sections.html:
Beatrice is the seat of Gage County, which borders Kansas on Nebraska's southern edge. Population has held steady: 21,704 at the 2020 census and an estimated 21,711 in 2025. The county has three cities, Beatrice, Blue Springs and Wymore, plus nine villages. Lincoln is the nearest large city for much of the county, about 40 miles north of Beatrice.

Housing units numbered 10,327 in 2020, with 10.1% vacant. Renters occupied nearly three in ten homes, so landlords make up a real share of sellers. A county settled this early describes parcels by legal description, and a title company will want to read that description and the recorded history before closing.

sections.h2: How the assessor values a home
sections.html:
For most homes the assessor starts from replacement cost new, subtracts depreciation, adds land, and then checks the result against sales within set market areas. Residential and commercial values aim for 92 to 100 percent of market value, and agricultural land for 69 to 75 percent.

Residential values rely on a two-year sales study, agricultural and commercial values on three years, and the study period ends June 30 of the preceding year. State law has the office review each property at least every six years. Field staff drive county vehicles and wear name badges and bright green vests.

  • A market neighborhood can include as many as 500 homes, so values are set by group, not by one sale.
  • Commercial property is often valued by an income approach, and income information sent to the office stays confidential.
  • Statements go to the address on line 19 of the Form 521 transfer statement filed with your deed.
  • Greenbelt status for qualifying farmland requires Form 456 before August 1.
  • Ask the assessor's office which market area your house falls in, since that group's sales drive the value.

You protest the valuation, never the tax itself. Form 422, in triplicate, goes to the County Board of Equalization through the county clerk's office at 612 Grant Street in Beatrice. Real property protests are due on or before June 30 and personal property protests by May 1. A protest that omits the requested value and the reasons can be dismissed.

The assessor's office suggests first asking an appraiser to explain how your value was reached, which gives the office a chance to fix errors. After a hearing, the board notifies you of its decision within seven days. If you still disagree, the Tax Equalization and Review Commission hears an appeal filed within 30 days of the board's adjournment; July 25 counts as that date for the June 1 to July 25 session.

What helps is a showing that your value sits above the market or out of step with similar properties.

sections.h2: Tax due dates and ways to pay
sections.html:
Both real estate and personal property bills are due December 31, and notices go out in December. Half becomes delinquent on May 1 of the next year and the rest on September 1, with delinquencies charged a 14 percent statutory rate.

The treasurer's office phone is (402) 223-1319. A wrong address can be fixed by phone or with the county's change of address form.

Mobile homes follow a few extra rules. The county doesn't prorate taxes on a sold mobile home, so buyer and seller must split them. A moving permit isn't issued until taxes are paid to date, and moving without that step is a class four misdemeanor. If the new owner never files forms 521 and 402, the tax statement stays in the seller's name.

sections.h2: How the Gage County tax sale works
sections.html:
Each March the treasurer runs a public tax sale at 9:00 a.m. in the third-floor district courtroom. The Beatrice Daily Sun carries the delinquent parcels for three consecutive weeks in February beforehand.

Bidders register in advance, pay a $25 registration fee, and take turns choosing parcels round-robin under Nebraska statute 77-1807. A buyer gets a tax lien, not the property. A certificate that isn't redeemed within three years opens the way to foreclosure, with strict notice deadlines before three years and nine months. Redemption pays the buyer 14 percent interest, and purchasers add an automatic $150 administrative fee for serving notice on the owner, which the owner pays at redemption.

Bankruptcy parcels and government-owned land never go to the sale. Owners who want to avoid the notice step and extra fees usually clear the balance or sell before the February advertising run.

Homestead exemption applicants, generally owners over 65 and certain disabled people, must file between February 1 and June 30 every year in the assessor's office. You lose the exemption if you sell or leave the home before August 15, though if you buy another Nebraska home before that date you can file a transfer statement to move it.

Closing brings the state documentary stamp tax: $3.32 on every $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026, owed by the seller as grantor. Zoning and building permits, including setbacks, are checked by legal description and address with county planning, and a permit application needs two identical sets of plans.

Added a garage, deck or finished space? Collect the permits before you list, since a title company or lender may ask.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
• Call the treasurer for your balance and ask whether the parcel is headed for the February advertising list.
  • Check which half of the bill is open, remembering the May 1 and September 1 delinquency dates.
  • Confirm that forms 521 and 402 were filed when you bought, so the statement and mailing address are right.
  • Collect permits for any addition, garage or deck.
  • If you claim a homestead exemption, remember it ends if you sell before August 15 unless you transfer it to another Nebraska home.
  • For a mobile home, settle with the buyer in writing how the taxes are split, since the county won't prorate them.

Sellers who work through this list usually learn the payoff figure before they talk to any buyer, and that makes comparing offers far easier.

sections.h2: Selling a Gage County house with taxes owed
sections.html:
A house on the tax sale list can still be sold if the delinquent taxes and charges are cleared at closing. Where a certificate has already been bought, redemption adds the buyer's interest and the $150 service fee. Your title company gets the payoff from the treasurer and deducts it from your proceeds.

Send Cash Home Buyers a Gage County address and we'll explain how an as-is offer would work. There are no showings or lender appraisals, which helps when the February advertising date is near. Ask the treasurer's office at (402) 223-1319 for the balance before you call us, if you can.

faqs.q: When are Gage County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 31. The first half is delinquent the following May 1 and the second half the following September 1, with a 14 percent statutory rate on delinquencies.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Gage County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Only the valuation, not the bill. Send Form 422 to the county clerk in Beatrice by June 30 for real property, naming the value you want and your reasons.

faqs.q: What fees apply when paying Gage County taxes by card?
faqs.a: Cards carry a 2.49 percent convenience fee and e-checks cost $1.75. Pay online at nto.us.

faqs.q: Does Gage County prorate taxes when a mobile home is sold?
faqs.a: No. Buyer and seller divide them. The new owner also files forms 521 and 402 with the assessor, or the statement keeps the seller's name.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gage County house that is on the tax sale list?
faqs.a: Yes, once delinquent taxes and charges are cleared at closing. When a certificate was already sold, redemption also costs the buyer's interest and a $150 service fee.
